entries.reason: whether the operation point chosen by a recall has a minimum precision. This port runs a Core ML classifier, which answers one score per class, and a precision and recall curve is those same scores swept across thresholds of themselves: there is no set of scores here and so no operation point to ask about
entries.effect: the method is there and answers NO, which is the answer to a question about a curve this port's classifications do not have
entries.source: the SDK header's own rule for the addition these three members belong to, which makes hasPrecisionRecallCurve the gate and says the other two must not be sent when it is NO, and this port's request path in VNHandlers.m, which builds one VNClassificationObservation per class from one score and keeps no scores of its own; facts/Vision/Absence.md section 5

entries.reason: whether the recogniser corrects the language of what it reads. Three things are known and none of them is Apple's default: the 16.4 header this package compiles against declares no default for it at all; neither 6.1.3 nor 4.3 can be asked, because neither carries a Vision image and so no release this port deploys on has a value to give; and nothing in this port ever sets the flag, because nothing here runs a text recognition -- the request path refuses VNRecognizeTextRequest with VNErrorNotImplemented before any recogniser stage exists to correct anything. So the value is whatever the initialiser left, and it is written down here rather than guessed
entries.effect: the property is there and answers NO. That is an answer about the port and the release together and not Apple's default: a caller reading NO must not take it for the value Apple's own Vision would give a request it can run, and a YES written in from memory would have been worse than either
entries.source: the port's own request built and the flag read on it, by tools/vision/conforms130.m compiled for Mac Catalyst, which answers NO; the absence of a declaration in the 16.4 header, read out of the header this package compiles against; and the Vision census of 6.1.3 and 4.3, which finds no image naming Vision in either; facts/Vision/Absence.md sections 1, 6 and 8

entries.reason: the progress a long request reports through. The build emits the protocol's metadata into the library, so the name resolves at run time. A class whose own SDK header names this protocol is put in the protocol's conformance list by the declaration alone -- declaring VNRecognizeTextRequest was enough, and no adoption was written anywhere -- so -conformsToProtocol: answers YES for the port's own text request whether or not this port wants it to, and the two members the protocol declares are written down in Vision130.m because of that
entries.effect: the protocol is there: NSProtocolFromString answers it by name, and the port's VNRecognizeTextRequest conforms to it and answers both of its members -- progressHandler hands back the block a caller installed and indeterminate answers NO. The handler is never called, because the request cannot be run here, which is what a request that reports no progress says
entries.source: the port's own classes built under names of their own and asked what they conform to, by tools/vision/conforms130.m compiled for Mac Catalyst, with a name that is no class at all asked as the control; and this host's own Vision, where NSProtocolFromString answers for the protocol and answers nil for a name it does not carry, by tools/vision/probe130.m; facts/Vision/Absence.md sections 4 and 8
